Decline
dē-klīn´
v. (to turn aside, bend away from a course; rendering Hebrew natah and sur)
Latin declinare, to bend away. The Hebrew is to stretch or turn aside; the Authorized Version's decline is a path left, not a strength lost.

Biblical Definition

“Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies” (Psa 119:157). The Law: “Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment” (Exo 23:2); of the priests' sentence, “thou shalt not decline from the sentence which they shall shew thee, to the right hand, nor to the left” (Deu 17:11). Solomon: “neither decline from the words of my mouth” (Pro 4:5); of the strange woman, “Let not thine heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths” (Pro 7:25).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines decline as to bend downward; to lean to one side; to deviate from a right line; to shun, to avoid; to fall, to decay.

expand to see more

DECLINE, v.i. To lean downward; to bend; to lean from a right line.

2. To deviate; to take a different direction; to depart from a fixed point or course.

3. To fall; to tend or draw towards the close; as, the day declines.

4. To decay; to be impaired; to tend to a less perfect state.

Key Scripture

Psa 119:157 — "Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies."

Exo 23:2 — "Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment:"

Deu 17:11 — "According to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, and according to the judgment which they shall tell thee, thou shalt do: thou shalt not decline from the sentence which they shall shew thee, to the right hand, nor to the left."

Pro 4:5 — "Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth."

Pro 7:25 — "Let not thine heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths."

Modern Corruption

The majority is treated as a moral authority, and the Law forbade declining after many before it forbade anything about the poor.

expand to see more

Exodus 23:2 is the earliest law against the crowd. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil — the number of people doing a thing is not evidence about the thing — and the second clause is the courtroom form of the same law: do not decline after many to wrest judgment. A man declines by degrees, not by decision; he bends toward where the weight is, and the weight is usually the many. Psalm 119:157 is the refusal stated in the first person, under pressure: persecutors and enemies in number, and the psalmist's yet. Proverbs 7:25 locates the decline before the act: let not thine heart decline to her ways — the path is left in the heart first, and the feet follow later, having already decided.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew natah (H5186), to stretch out, turn aside, decline; sur (H5493), to turn aside, depart.

expand to see more

Hebrew natah (H5186) — to turn aside, decline; Psalm 119:51, 119:157, Exodus 23:2, Proverbs 4:5, 7:25, Job 23:11.

Hebrew sur (H5493) — to turn aside, depart; Deuteronomy 17:11, 2 Chronicles 34:2.

Usage

"“Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many” — the crowd is not evidence."

"“Yet do I not decline from thy testimonies” — the refusal, under pressure."

"“Let not thine heart decline to her ways” — the path left in the heart first."
